lore.content:
# Pierre's General Store

## What it is

The town's shop, on the west side of the square, and the ground floor of a family home. Seeds, saplings, fertiliser, groceries, cooking oil, flour, sugar, a rack of wallpaper and flooring samples, a bouquet under glass for anyone who has decided something, and a bulletin of local prices. Pierre buys produce and foraged goods over the counter at a margin she will cheerfully admit to.

## The place itself

Counter facing the door, shelves close together, a chill cabinet of fresh vegetables, and the town calendar on the wall where birthdays and festival dates are written up — the reason half the town comes in without buying anything. Nine in the morning to five in the afternoon, historically shut one day a week; if the warehouse store has come and gone, Pierre works seven days out of a mix of duty and dread. On the rare day she closes anyway there is a money box on the counter and a note in her handwriting.

Behind and above the shop is the family's home: kitchen, Abigail's room with the spirit board and the game console, Caroline's exercise cupboard, a shelf of books that includes one on surviving a difficult daughter and one titled *Why JojaCo Must Be Stopped*. Off the back is Caroline's sunroom, kept warm and green all year, with her tea crop in it. A guinea pig named David lives in a cage in Abigail's room.

## Who is there

Pierre behind the counter through the working day. Caroline in and out, more often in the sunroom or the vegetable patch. Abigail upstairs, or not at home at all. Half the town passes through in any given week, and Pierre hears everything first.

## Roleplay notes

This is the town's information exchange as much as its shop. A conversation across the counter reaches four other households by evening. Pierre's business anxiety, Caroline's separate green world at the back, and Abigail's need for a door she can shut all live in one building, which is most of the tension in that family. Prices, stock, and opening hours are soft — do not run a shop inventory.

lore.name: Railroad and Spa
lore.keys: railroad, the tracks, train platform, the spa, bath house, hot spring, the summit, đường sắt, đường ray, sân ga, nhà tắm, suối nước nóng, khu tắm nước nóng, đỉnh núi
lore.content:
# Railroad and Spa

## What it is

The high shelf above the mountain: a stretch of railway line, a public bath house built over a hot spring, and a path further up to the valley's summit. The tracks were buried by a rockslide for years and can be walked once the way is clear.

## The place itself

A single line of track running east to west along the cliff with a small platform, a dumpster, a recycling bin, and a box on the platform that has held stranger things than post. Trains pass. They do not stop. Sometimes something falls off one.

Set into the hillside is the bath house — free, open at all hours, warm, and the only building in the valley that is nobody's home and nobody's business. A tiled entry, changing rooms either side, and a steaming pool through the far door. It is the one place in the valley where everyone undresses in front of everyone and nobody comments on it.

At the west end, a boulder blocks a path until somebody clears it. Beyond it the ground climbs to the summit — bare rock, wind, and the whole valley laid out below. On the east side, a cave mouth stands sealed by magic; the seal was put there deliberately and by someone still living.

## Who is there

Nobody, mostly. Linus walks the line in autumn and uses the bath house in winter because even she needs to be warm indoors sometimes. Penny comes here after dark when she wants to be somewhere that is not the trailer, and has left a note asking someone to meet her. Emily and Maru use it in the cold months. Someone lost a necklace out here and has not told her mother.

## Roleplay notes

The bath house is the valley's honest room: hot water, bare skin, tired people, no audience. The railroad is for arrivals, departures, and things that come from outside. The summit is where the valley is looked at from a distance, and it means something to whoever is standing there.

lore.name: River Road
lore.keys: river road, 1 river road, 2 river road, the trailer, george and evelyn's house, pam's trailer, đường ven sông, con đường bờ sông, nhà di động, xe kéo của pam, căn nhà bên sông, nhà của evelyn
lore.content:
# River Road

Two houses on the east bank of the river in Pelican Town, and about as far apart in circumstances as the valley gets.

## 1 River Road — George, Evelyn and Alex

A tidy house that has absorbed thirty years of one couple's life. A radio on the oldies station, a well-stocked fridge, an oven that smells of baking, a book called *Cookies For Every Season*, another called *Dealing With Loss*, and a coal miner's memoir on George's shelf beside her chair by the window. Ramps and a wheelchair's turning space worked into rooms that were not built for them.

Alex's room is a shrine to a career that does not exist yet: a polished gridball helmet, a ball, a thirty-pound weight, a muscle magazine, a box of trading cards, hair gel, and a stats-and-standings volume for last season. In a drawer there is a letter from her mother, written knowing she was dying, asking her own mother to take care of Alex because she needs a family and something stable, and telling both of them she loves them. Everyone in this house has read it and nobody mentions it.

Out front, Alex's dog Dusty sleeps in a box.

## 2 River Road — Pam and Penny

A cramped metal trailer with a messy yard, close enough to the water to hear it. Inside: a couch, a television, a microwave, and a bin full of empty bottles. Penny's corner of it holds a teacher's guidebook, a fantasy novel, a fantasy epic she reads for pleasure, and a book of fairy tales about junimos and other fables. She does the cleaning, the cooking, and the household arithmetic.

Pam drove the town's bus for years and drove trucks before that; when the bus broke down she lost the work and the days lost their shape. If the bus ever runs again she comes back to life, and if enough money ever comes through this door the trailer gets replaced by an actual house, which changes how Pam carries herself in public and does not fix anything underneath.

## Roleplay notes

One house grieving and comfortable; one house tight and strained. The two households sit on the same road and the contrast is the point. Do not treat the trailer upgrade or the bus repair as scheduled events; both are live possibilities.

lore.name: Stardrop Saloon
lore.keys: stardrop saloon, the saloon, the bar, the pub, drinks, dish of the day, quán rượu, quán bar, quán stardrop, đi uống, đồ uống, món đặc biệt hôm nay
lore.content:
# Stardrop Saloon

## What it is

The only bar in the valley and the room where the whole town eventually ends up. Gus owns it, cooks in it, and runs the counter from midday until midnight. Emily works the floor most evenings.

## The place itself

One large room: bar along one side with the kitchen behind it, tables and booths, a pool table nobody plays seriously, a jukebox, a cola machine that takes coins and gives nothing worth having, and two arcade cabinets in the corner — a punishing cowboy shooter and a minecart game — that Abigail and Sam treat as a standing competition. A chalked dish of the day changes daily and is genuinely good. There is beer, coffee, an espresso strong enough to be a dare, pizza, salad, spaghetti, omelettes, pancakes, hashbrowns, maki rolls, crab cakes, and bread.

Out the back there is a bin, and the day's unsold dish sometimes ends up in it still edible, which is not lost on anyone who needs it.

## Who is there

Gus behind the bar. Emily on the floor. Shane on a stool by the counter most nights, drinking steadily. Pam on the stool she considers hers, with a tab. Clint at the same table, alone, watching Emily and saying nothing. Marnie in the evening because animals are not enough company. Willy, Lewis one night a week for the news, Harvey rarely and awkwardly, Abigail and Sam and Sebastian at the arcade or a booth. George comes up when there is a game on and it makes her feel lively.

## Life here

Loud in the evening and dead in the afternoon. The town's news, feuds, and confessions all pass through this room, usually in the wrong order. Somebody is always slightly drunker than they meant to be. Gus notices and manages it without comment.

## Roleplay notes

The best place in the valley for an unplanned encounter, an overheard remark, or a conversation that goes further than intended. Hours are soft — if a scene wants the saloon open, it is open. Do not narrate a menu; narrate what the room is like tonight.

lore.name: The Blacksmith
lore.keys: blacksmith, the forge, clint's shop, tool upgrade, geodes, sell ore, anvil, tiệm rèn, lò rèn, thợ rèn, tiệm của clint, nâng cấp dụng cụ, bán quặng, cái đe
lore.content:
# The Blacksmith

## What it is

The forge on the east side of Pelican Town, a family trade going back generations, and Clint's whole life whether she wanted it or not. Open through the working day, roughly nine until four.

## The place itself

Hot, dark, and loud. A professional furnace with molten metal turning over inside it, an anvil made of iridium alloy that Clint is quietly proud of, a soot-choked hearth, a rack of tongs, and a stack of metalworking blueprints. The counter takes tools for upgrading — a fee, the right ore, and a wait of a day or two — buys ore and coal, and cracks geodes open for anyone who brings them and wants to know what is inside.

Her living space is behind the work. A tape of blues in the player. Aprons folded in a drawer with some magazines, an old sword, and a framed photograph of her mother. In the corner, a crumpled letter to Emily that says she knows Emily thinks of her as a friend, that it is her own fault for being too shy, and that she will never have the courage to say it out loud. She wrote it to herself and threw it away without sending it.

## Who is there

Clint, at the forge, apologetic and sweating and glad of the noise. Anyone with a broken tool or a bag of ore. Marlon comes about blades and haggles. Emily does not come here, which is the problem.

## Life here

Work she is good at, in a trade she did not choose, in a room she rarely leaves except to sit alone in the saloon and look at the barmaid. She talks about the weather, the price of ore, and her mother. She does not talk about the letter.

## Roleplay notes

Use the forge for craft, heat, physical competence, and the specific ache of a woman who is articulate about metal and mute about everything else. Do not run upgrade timers or a price list.

lore.name: The Farm
lore.keys: the farm, the old farm, the farmhouse, the fields, the greenhouse, the shipping bin, farmland, nông trại, nhà nông trại, nông trại cũ, cánh đồng, ruộng, nhà kính, thùng giao hàng, đất nông trại
lore.content:
# The Farm

## What it is

The old farmstead west of the bus stop and north of the forest: a few acres, a small cottage, and whatever the last generation left standing. It has been empty long enough for the fields to go to grass, brush and fallen wood, and the town has strong feelings about it either way.

## The place itself

A one-room cottage with a hearth, a bed, and a mailbox by the door. Outside: a shipping bin the mayor empties on her nightly round, a stone-lined well, and land in every direction — tillable ground, tree stands, boulders, a stream depending on which corner of the valley the plot lies in. The valley has several old holdings like this and they differ: one runs to river and gravel, one to forest and stumps, one to open hillside with ore in it, one down onto sand.

Behind the house, a cave in the hillside — cool, dark, and useful to whoever decides what to do with it. Below the kitchen, a cellar. Up the slope, the frame of a greenhouse with its glass gone, standing in ruins until somebody rebuilds it. Somewhere in the trees there is a small stone shrine the family left, addressed to a grandchild, with instructions and a date.

## What it gives

Whatever is put into it. Wild ground turns up coal, stone and stray seed; the untended parts spread weeds fast and swallow the paths again over winter. Buildings — coop, barn, shed, mill, extension — are Robin's work and Robin's fee.

## Life here

Solitary by nature and social by accident: Robin turns up with timber, Marnie about a stray animal, Willy about a fishing spot, Lewis about the bin, and Pierre about anything she can sell you. The bus stop is a short walk east, so the whole valley passes near the gate.

## Roleplay notes

Do not assume the user farms this land or owns it. It may be theirs, a neighbour's, abandoned, half-restored, or simply the place they walk past. Do not track crops, seasons, or money unless the story asks for them.

lore.name: The Mines
lore.keys: the mines, the mine, mine shaft, the caves, underground, down the mine, mine levels, hầm mỏ, khu mỏ, trong mỏ, giếng mỏ, hang động, xuống mỏ, tầng mỏ
lore.content:
# The Mines

## What it is

An abandoned commercial mine cut into the mountainside above the lake, and the only genuinely dangerous place in the valley that anyone visits on purpose. It goes down a hundred and twenty levels and nobody has found a floor beneath that. Marlon's guild sits at the entrance because someone has to.

## The place itself

A timbered shaft, a lift cage that still works and remembers which floors you have reached, and level after level of worked-out rock. The character of it changes with depth: dirt and stone near the surface, then cold and ice through the middle, then heat and dark red rock deep down. Ore in the walls — copper, iron, gold, and further down things the blacksmith will only see a few times in her life. Geodes to be cracked, gems in seams, and old ladders that go down further than they should.

Things live down there. Slimes in every colour, bats, cave insects, animated stone, crab-like things that sit still until they do not, skeletons in the deep levels, ghosts in the cold ones. Nobody argues about whether the monsters are real; you can hear them.

At the bottom of the last level, someone eventually finds a key shaped like a skull. It fits a door in the desert.

## Who is there

Marlon at the entrance, selling weapons, boots and rings, keeping a bounty board, and running a paid retrieval service for the possessions of people who did not walk out under their own power. Gil in the chair behind her, asleep. Clint buys ore from anyone who brings it up, and has cleared monsters herself exactly as many times as she claims. Abigail practices with a sword and goes in further than her parents know. Somewhere much deeper, a small figure with a lamp trades with anyone who can understand what she says, and she is not human.

## Life here

Cold air out of the entrance, water dripping, the lift chain rattling. People go in for ore, for money, for nerve, or to prove something, and a few come out worse. Marlon sweeps the area in the small hours and has carried more than one unconscious stranger home. Linus has done the same, without being asked and without mentioning it afterwards.

## Roleplay notes

Real danger, real consequence: injury, exhaustion, getting lost, needing help. Do not run mine levels as a progression system or track loot. The valley's older strangeness — dwarves, an earlier civilisation, whatever the deep floors are — lives down here and should stay half-explained.

lore.name: The Mountain
lore.keys: the mountain, mountain road, mountain lake, the quarry, up the mountain, north of town, ngọn núi, trên núi, đường lên núi, hồ trên núi, hồ nước, mỏ đá, phía bắc thị trấn
lore.content:
# The Mountain

## What it is

The high ground north of Pelican Town: pine forest, a cold lake, a working mine, a quarry, and the two buildings that sit up here because their business needs to. Three separate paths climb out of the north edge of town and all of them are a proper climb.

## The place itself

The lake is the centre of it — deep, cold, ringed with rock, with a wooden platform out over the water that is the best fishing spot in the valley. The carpenter's house and shop stand on the road above the lake's west side. East and up, the old mine entrance is cut into the rock, with the adventurer's guild in the building beside it and a minecart track running down toward town. Higher again and east, the quarry: bare stone, standing water, and ore near the surface.

On the slope above the lake, near the water, Linus keeps a tent, a firepit and a life she chose. It is not a hardship post and she does not treat it as one.

A section of the lakeside was buried by a landslide once, from corporate drilling nobody consented to; the company cleared it, called the operation entirely legal, and apologised for the inconvenience.

## What it gives

Leeks and horseradish in spring, spice berries and wild grapes in summer, mushrooms, wild plums and hazelnuts in autumn, holly and crystal fruit in winter. Coal and copper turn up in the loose ground. The lake holds largemouth bass, carp, bullhead, sturgeon in summer, and a legendary spring fish nobody has landed twice.

## Life here

Quiet, cold, and busy in a way the town is not: hammering from Robin's shop, someone hauling ore down the path, a light on in the guild after dark, smoke from a tent. Winter up here is serious.

## Roleplay notes

The mountain is where people go to work or to be left alone. Distances feel longer in bad weather, and the walk back down is when conversations actually happen.

lore.name: Willow Lane
lore.keys: willow lane, 1 willow lane, 2 willow lane, jodi's house, haley and emily's house, west side of town, đường willow, nhà của jodi, nhà của haley và emily, phía tây thị trấn, hai căn nhà bên kia sông
lore.content:
# Willow Lane

Two houses side by side on the west side of Pelican Town, across the river from the square.

## 1 Willow Lane — Jodi, Kent and Sam

A small family house kept immaculately by a woman who never finishes. A kitchen with something always on the stove, a fridge holding eggs, bread, carrots and milk, and a radio tuned to the news. Jodi cooks seriously and well and has won a competition with a recipe of her own.

Sam has the biggest bedroom and treats it as a studio: an electric guitar with active pickups and a whammy bar, guitar picks and spare skateboard wheels in a drawer, skate magazines, a paperback about UFO mysteries, a computer full of games, and industrial quantities of extra-strong hair gel. Vincent's room is small and strewn with hobby materials, and there is a progress report on the wall that says she could do with studying more.

In a drawer there is a letter Kent wrote from overseas before coming home, warning Jodi that she might not be the woman she remembered. Jodi kept it. Kent is home now, waking before dawn with nothing to do, and the house has not settled around her yet.

## 2 Willow Lane — Emily and Haley

The house their parents left in their care while they travel; postcards arrive from cruises and distant coasts and the invitation to come along is always open and always declined. The last letter came from the Fern Islands after two months there.

Downstairs is Emily's: a bolt of blue cloth with pieces cut out of it and embroidery along the fringe, a password-protected computer, a shelf of gemstones, a book on street fashion in Zuzu City, another on modern dance, and a potted plant with a note on it reading *something to remember me by* signed by Sandy. The oven smells of cupcakes; the fridge holds cupcakes, milk, a tightly sealed jar of cornichons and quinoa salad.

Haley's room is a deluxe vanity buried under creams and powders, a locked diary that is empty, a globe with the valley marked on it, a fashion magazine, a book on building your own darkroom from scratch, and her camera — which starts as a hobby and becomes the thing she is serious about. Her great-grandmother's bracelet is the one possession she would be devastated to lose.

## Roleplay notes

Two households built on absence: one waiting for a soldier to become a wife again, one raising itself while its parents sail. Good for domestic scenes, sisterly friction, and Jodi's exhausting competence. Do not treat the parents' return as scheduled.

lore.name: Wizard's Tower and the Sewers
lore.keys: wizard's tower, the tower, rasmodius, the sewers, sewer, under the town, witch's swamp, tòa tháp, tháp phù thủy, cống ngầm, đường cống, dưới thị trấn, đầm phù thủy
lore.content:
# Wizard's Tower and the Sewers

## The tower

A stone tower in the trees at the west end of Cindersap Forest, behind a low wall, up a path most of the town will not walk. The door is locked and you can hear someone inside. Open from early morning until late at night to anyone she has decided to admit.

Inside: a cauldron working over a fire, shelves of reagents, a desk of charts and correspondence, furniture that all matches because she made ethereal copies of it after her ex-wife took the originals, and a shrine of illusions that will change a visitor's appearance for a fee. A hatch in the floor leads to a basement she opens only for people she trusts, where the real work happens.

Rasmodius has lived here longer than most of the valley has been alive. She chose the valley for its magic rather than its scenery, communes with elementals in storms, keeps the town at arm's length, and knows exactly what is living in the old community hall. Her ex-wife is a witch beyond a sealed passage on the railroad, has become something monstrous, and holds property of hers that she will not go and reclaim herself. She is watching the valley's adult women for an apprentice whether or not they know it.

Caroline used to walk up here often, and does not discuss it.

## The sewers

Under the town, reached by a hatch in the graveyard or a pipe surfacing in the forest, both of which need a rusted key. Brick corridors, standing water, and a persistent green smell.

Two things live down here. One is a shadow-person, a courteous merchant of rare and exotic goods who is startled that a human would visit and will trade with anyone who is decent about it. Deeper in, past a force-field the Wizard put up, a small figure with a lamp and a language of her own trades with anyone who can understand her. The two of them were enemies for a long time; the Wizard brokered peace between them and considers both of them people.

There is also a stone dog on a plinth called the Statue of Uncertainty, which will change the shape of a life for ten thousand gold and says *woof* when it is done.

## Roleplay notes

This is the valley's magic, and it should stay oblique: real, consequential, and never a solution. The Wizard can be wrong, evasive, or self-serving. The sewer dwellers are people, not monsters, and the town's fear of them is the town's problem. Do not run quests, keys, or gated access as mechanics.

lore.name: Forest Cottages
lore.keys: leah's cottage, leah's cabin, elliott's cabin, the beach cabin, the ruined house, sewer pipe, nhà gỗ của leah, căn nhà gỗ, nhà nhỏ ven biển, chòi trên bãi biển, căn nhà đổ nát, ống cống
lore.content:
# The Two Cabins

The valley's two artists both live in one room at the edge of things, and both are broke.

## Leah's cottage

A single-room cabin in Cindersap Forest beside the river, small, cluttered, and smelling of cedar. A work in progress on the bench, a half-finished wooden sculpture with the wood still fresh, a stack of her paintings — mostly landscapes and studies of things she found outside — and two books on the shelf: one a practical guide to living off the land, the other about dealing with overbearing people, which is not there by accident.

She left a city apartment and a long relationship to come here, because her partner wanted her to give up art for something respectable and she was not willing. She carves and hammers and sands at all hours, and the sound carries across the water. Money is thin: she forages most of her fresh food and eats a lot of bread in winter. There is a telephone on the wall that almost never has a message on it.

If her work ever starts selling — a local show she has to be talked into, and later a small mail-order trade — everything changes except the cabin.

## Elliott's cabin

A one-room shack on the sand at the west end of Pelican Beach, on the tide line, with the damp in the walls. Dark, spider-ridden, and half full of sand. The writing desk is the centre of the world: covered in notes and crumpled paper, a novel in progress with no guarantee it will amount to anything. A painting by Leah on the wall. A bonsai she is trying to grow and a mini-palm imported from the desert, both doing better than expected. An empty cubby she has plans for. A piano she plays a little, having done since she was small, as her only allowed recreation.

She combs the beach for shells, keeps a rose alive with mixed success, and eventually drags an abandoned rowboat out of the sand and makes it float.

## Roleplay notes

Two households built on the same bet: that the work matters more than the security. Good for scenes about money, doubt, and other people's opinions of an artist's life. The two of them like each other and read each other's work.

lore.name: Ginger Island
lore.keys: ginger island, the island, the boat, the resort, the volcano, tropical, south sea, hòn đảo, đảo ginger, con thuyền, khu nghỉ dưỡng, núi lửa, nhiệt đới, biển nam
lore.content:
# Ginger Island

## What it is

A tropical island far to the south, reachable only by boat from the back room of Willy's fish shop, and only once that boat is seaworthy. Nobody in the valley talks about it much, because almost nobody has been.

## The place itself

Permanent summer, jungle, black sand, and parrots everywhere. A dock on the south shore where the boat ties up, and a stretch of beach nearby that somebody eventually turns into a small resort — sun loungers, a bar, and whichever valley women feel like making the trip. West, open farmland worth planting, a farmhouse, a shipwreck on the rocks, a grove where the slimes are striped like cats, and a cave with an enormous frog in it that wants to be fed. East, a hut in the jungle. South-east, a cove with a wrecked ship and something living in it. North, a dig site, a survey tent staffed by a very earnest naturalist, an island trader who takes no money, and a volcano with a working forge inside it and a river of lava.

Golden walnuts are hidden all over the island — buried, in barrels, taken by monsters, in the volcano — and something on the island is counting them.

An adult woman lives here alone in the jungle, raised by parrots, who speaks to them more easily than to people. She comes to the valley eventually, learns the local wild food from Linus, calls her aunt, and studies with Penny alongside other adult residents.

## Life here

Heat, birds, and green. When the resort is open the valley treats it as a holiday and behaves accordingly: less clothing, more drinking, and conversations that would not happen at home. Gus runs the bar. Everyone is looser here and nobody says so.

## Roleplay notes

Optional and distant — the island exists whether or not a story goes there. Use it for holiday scenes, for the outside world, and for the valley's women away from everyone who knows them. Do not gate it behind the boat repair, and do not run walnut counts.

lore.name: Secret Woods
lore.keys: secret woods, the deep woods, the hidden clearing, old growth, hardwood stumps, rừng bí mật, rừng sâu, khoảng trống ẩn trong rừng, rừng nguyên sinh, gốc cây gỗ cứng
lore.content:
# Secret Woods

## What it is

A small pocket of old-growth forest through a gap at the far west edge of Cindersap, behind fallen timber that has to be cut before anyone can get in. Once you are through, it is quiet in a way the rest of the valley is not.

## The place itself

Enormous trees, a canopy that keeps the ground in green half-light, standing water, and hardwood stumps that come back every few days. Slimes wander here in the open, which nowhere else in the valley does. Mushrooms everywhere — morels and common mushrooms in spring, red mushrooms and fiddlehead fern in summer, chanterelles in autumn — and holly under winter.

In a clearing at the back there is an old statue of a woman holding a plate, worn by weather, inscribed for an old master of sweets who is still searching for the sweetest taste. Nobody knows who put it there. There is a small pool with woodskip in it, a fish that lives nowhere else in the valley.

## Life here

Almost nobody comes. Foragers who know about it come for the mushrooms; Linus knows every inch of it; Leah walks here for the shapes in the timber. A secret note in hurried spelling once asked someone to bring maple syrup here, and whoever wrote it was not human.

## Roleplay notes

Use this for privacy, for the uncanny, and for the valley's older layer — the parts that predate the town. It rewards being alone. Do not treat the hardwood, the mushrooms, or the locked door as gated content; they are scenery and mystery.

lore.name: Valley Festivals
lore.keys: festival, festivals, the calendar, town event, holiday, celebration, seasonal event, lễ hội, các lễ hội, lịch, sự kiện trong thị trấn, ngày lễ, lễ kỷ niệm, sự kiện theo mùa
lore.content:
# Valley Festivals

## What they are

Eight fixed festivals across the four seasons, plus a handful of multi-day gatherings, and they are the only occasions when the whole valley reliably stands in one place at one time. Every shop closes. Everyone comes, including the ones who complain about coming. The mayor organises them, takes credit for them, and frets about how they look to outsiders. Gus cooks for nearly all of them, for days beforehand, and hands it out free.

They matter more than their size suggests. This is a town of about thirty women who see each other constantly and know each other far too well, and a festival is the one structure that puts them in costume, in competition, in a dance, or in the dark together, with an excuse.

## The calendar

- **Egg Festival** — spring 13, the town square, morning to mid-afternoon. Egg hunt, eggs cooked every way there is, spiked punch.
- **Desert Festival** — spring 15 to 17, Calico Desert, from mid-morning. Three days, if the bus is running.
- **Flower Dance** — spring 24, a clearing in Cindersap Forest. Partners, a stilted formal dance, a flower queen.
- **Luau** — summer 11, the beach. A communal soup and a visiting dignitary who tastes it first.
- **Trout Derby** — summer 20 and 21, the river. Two days, no ceremony.
- **Dance of the Moonlight Jellies** — summer 28, the beach, after dark. A candle-boat and the jellies coming in.
- **Stardew Valley Fair** — fall 16, the town square. The big one: grange displays, games, tokens, a fortune teller, tourists.
- **Spirit's Eve** — fall 27, the town square, from ten at night. A haunted maze built in secret, caged monsters, pumpkin ale.
- **Festival of Ice** — winter 8, the frozen lake in the forest. Snow sculpture and an ice fishing contest. No food.
- **SquidFest** — winter 12 and 13, the beach. Two days of squid and visiting anglers.
- **Night Market** — winter 15 to 17, the pier, from evening. A merchant fleet in port for three nights.
- **Feast of the Winter Star** — winter 25, the town square. A spirit tree, a secret gift exchange, and a legend.

## How the town treats them

A letter from the mayor arrives the day before, and one a week early for the fair. Something goes up on the notice board. Attendance is not optional in practice: the whole day is given over, and anyone who stays home is discussed.

The same people behave the same way every year, and everyone knows it — who wins, who sulks, who drinks too much, who has been practising, who says she hates it and comes anyway. That repetition is the point. Half the town's affection runs on it.

## Roleplay notes

Festivals are opportunities, not appointments. Nothing requires the calendar to be tracked, no festival has to happen on cue, and one can be recent memory, imminent, or in progress as the story needs. Individual entries describe what each one is like; use them for crowd texture, for putting two people beside each other who would not otherwise stand together, and for the specific licence a costume, a contest, or a dark beach gives. Outcomes are never fixed — contests can be lost, dances refused, gifts badly chosen.

lore.keys: desert festival, calico eggs, calico egg, spring 15, spring 16, spring 17, the races, lễ hội sa mạc, hội chợ sa mạc, trứng calico, cuộc đua, giải đua, sa mạc calico
lore.content:
# Desert Festival

## What it is

Spring 15, 16 and 17, out in Calico Desert, from mid-morning each day. Three days, and the only festival that takes the valley out of the valley — which means it happens only if the bus is running. It has been a tradition for as long as anyone can remember and it stopped for years when the bus broke down. Getting it back is the single most popular thing anyone has ever done here, and the mayor thanks whoever managed it every time she sees them.

Everything is free. The whole town comes out into permanent summer with the sand hot through their shoes, and stays for three days.

## What happens out there

**The eggs.** Calico eggs — palm-sized, patterned, worthless as food — turn up all over the sand and in the caverns, and for three days they are the local currency. Nobody accepts money for anything; they accept eggs. This is the whole economy of the festival and people take it seriously enough to bargain hard over a handful.

**The stalls.** Two townspeople are picked each day to run a stall out of whatever they happen to own, which produces the best social document of the year: Abigail selling things out of her own closet, Sam offering a broken skateboard with a straight face, Leah's mini bookcases, Harvey's model aeroplanes, Maru's spare iridium, Marnie's leftover roll of wallpaper, Jodi apologising for her selection, Evelyn happy to sit there all day, Pam clearing old bottles out of the back of the fridge, Shane's freezer contents with a warning about the dates, George claiming to have everything worth selling. Pierre sells eggs for cash and asks you not to tell the mayor.

**The races.** Five racers — a rooster, a hornet, a shoe-shaped something, a snail, a cactus crawler — an announcer who works the crowd, and open betting on the winner. There is also a woman at the edge of the crowd who will fix a race for one egg and makes a phone call afterwards. The snail winning is a running joke and the announcer has never recovered from it.

**The food.** Gus is off duty for the first time all year and delighted about it. A chef with an unsettling manner will build you something to order from a short list of ingredients and sauces and then name the result — *Nachos Of The Desert*, *Warrior Smoothie*, *Smell Of The Sea* — and hand it over. There is a spicy tent that George makes straight for. Twelve soda flavours, which Shane intends to get through all of.

**The rest.** A scholar with a quiz and a prize for anyone who answers four questions about the valley. A woman giving away small cacti to anyone she decides is ready for the responsibility. A makeover stand where Emily or Sandy will rebuild your whole look and hand your old clothes back in a bag. The Adventurer's Guild sets up a challenge booth — Marlon offering a pair of dares each day, Gil awake for once and grading whatever you drag out of the Skull Cavern. Willy runs desert fishing challenges from the dry riverbed and pays in eggs.

## Who is where

Sandy calls it the busiest weekend of her year and means it as joy — she sees everyone she knows in three days and then does not see them again. Emily is at the makeover stand and gets to spend actual time with her. Robin stands around talking to neighbours she never sees. Haley oils herself and commits fully to the desert. Elliott has become a connoisseur of sand and will explain. Linus rides out under the bus. Kent is out in the open, in heat, being asked whether she is enjoying it. Harvey stays all day in case somebody does something stupid in the caverns and cheerfully tells you she would advise against it.

## Roleplay notes

Three days, so it is the one festival with room for a whole story rather than an afternoon. The heat, the distance from home, and the free food loosen everyone — this is where people say things they would not say in the square. Whether the bus runs is a live question and a good hook. The egg economy is a texture, not a system: nobody needs to count.

lore.name: Egg Festival
lore.keys: egg festival, egg hunt, spring 13, deviled eggs, easter, lễ hội trứng, đi tìm trứng, săn trứng, hội trứng, lễ phục sinh
lore.content:
# Egg Festival

## What it is

Spring 13, the town square, morning until mid-afternoon. The first festival of the year and the one everybody treats as the season opening: pastel bunting over the cobbles, a stall run out of the square, and a decorated egg on every flat surface. Gus has been cooking for days and everything on the table is eggs — fried, boiled, poached, deviled, scrambled, chocolate — plus a fruit punch that Pam has done something to and asked you not to mention.

## The egg hunt

The centrepiece. The mayor makes a speech about how efficiently the town's participants collect eggs compared with how they collect litter, tells everyone to calm down, asks whether everyone is ready, and starts it. Then the square is chaos for a couple of minutes: coloured eggs hidden in the flower beds, behind the benches, under the notice board, and grown women moving faster than they would like witnessed. Abigail has loved it for years, wins it more often than not, and has begun to wonder aloud whether she is too old for it — she is not going to stop. The winner gets a prize handed over with ceremony and the mayor thanks everyone for coming.

Nobody plays entirely fair. Willy hides an egg so well some years that nobody finds it until the summer heat brings out the smell. There used to be a rotten egg toss; the mayor put an end to that with some speed. Jas and Vincent have won it once between them by pooling what they found.

## Who is where

Emily is up before dawn colouring eggs and considers that the best part of the season; some years she sews tiny hats and trousers for a few of them. Marnie takes the whole thing as a credit to her hens and says so. Shane's birds have been laying overtime and she thinks they have earned an evening of sweet corn. Caroline watches Abigail and remembers her at four. Evelyn calls the tradition older than she is and means the comfort of it. Linus turns up quietly, late, for the food, and says plainly that nobody talks to her; she is after the deviled eggs and the pie. Sam's allergies ruin it for her every single year. Pierre is behind her booth and will bark at anyone who wanders round the back of it.

There is a photograph stand with a bunny theme that Haley uses. Demetrius finds the eating of eggs conceptually strange and one year contributes a carp roe pie on a technicality. Alex eats a dozen too many and regrets it. Sebastian remembers the egg toss fondly. George complains, then admits the smoked food is not bad.

## Roleplay notes

Bright, silly, and warm — the least loaded festival of the year, which makes it a good place to put two people who need an easy first afternoon. The hunt gives anyone permission to be undignified in public. The punch gives them permission to be honest. Who wins is not fixed, and neither is whether the hunt happens at all: the square works perfectly well as an ordinary spring party.

lore.name: Feast of the Winter Star
lore.keys: feast of the winter star, winter star, winter 25, secret gift, spirit tree, christmas, tiệc sao mùa đông, sao mùa đông, quà bí mật, tặng quà bí mật, trao đổi quà, cây linh hồn, giáng sinh
lore.content:
# Feast of the Winter Star

## What it is

Winter 25, the town square under snow, morning until mid-afternoon. The last festival of the year and the warmest: long tables set out in the cold, a decorated spirit tree with presents heaped under it and an overflow pile beside it, and the whole valley eating until it cannot move. The mayor says it is a day to be thankful for the year's good fortune, to forget your worries, and to relax, and for once nobody argues with her.

Gus cooks on a scale she does not attempt at any other time and will talk at length about her candy canes if allowed: the premier ones coloured with island ringfruit for that natural red, the standard peppermint batch, and the deluxe double-canes whose secret is a drop of vanilla in the white to complement the cherry — told under a promise of absolute secrecy, at length, until whoever she has cornered begins to sag. There is cinnamon nog, mulled wine, spiced cider with more fizz than Elliott expects, pecan pie, and green mint jelly Demetrius interrogates on principle.

Caroline, Marnie and Jodi decorate the tree together and call it a tradition worth keeping. Emily and Haley used to decorate cookies at this festival years ago and Emily thinks they should do it again, because you cannot let a good tradition die.

## The secret gift exchange

The mayor writes a week early with everyone's assignment: each woman in town is paired at random with another, told to tell nobody, and expected to arrive with something chosen for that person. Then the gifts change hands in the square, in front of everyone, and the whole social ledger of the town is read out loud in what people picked for each other.

It goes wrong as often as it goes right. Someone gets a corporate gift basket and is visibly insulted. Robin's wife buys her a power saw and has forgotten she bought her the same saw two years ago. Demetrius expects another tool set and sighs. Shane has been putting frozen pizzas under the tree because the weather does the work. Alex is fairly sure there is a gridball-shaped parcel with her name on it. Haley hopes for a camera. Clint would settle for new tools, hers having gone rusty. Abigail wonders which one is hers and hopes it is the big box. Jas and Vincent want to open presents now.

The person you are given may be someone you barely speak to. That is the interesting part.

## The legend

Willy will ask whether you want to hear the Legend of the Winter Star, and tell it if you say yes: in the winter night sky there is a bright star visible only from this valley, and nobody knows why. People once came from far away to see it, believing anyone who laid eyes on it would be blessed with good fortune. Some say the stardrop — the fruit that is not quite a fruit — is connected to it somehow. The Wizard says the mysterious Winter Star is one of the reasons she chose this valley for her research, and does not elaborate. Emily points at a decoration, calls it the Winter Star, and then admits her mistake, laughing.

## Who is where

The tables sort the town into families, which exposes who has one. Robin invites anyone without company to join her family's table. Evelyn extends the same invitation to anyone standing alone. Clint looks at all the happy families and says quietly that for her it is another lonely year. Linus says she would join in but does not think she is welcome — and then, some years, the mayor invites her to her own table personally and Linus cannot turn that down, which is the single kindest thing Lewis does all year. Leo stays out with Linus to keep her company when she will not come, and the two of them have their own small feast.

Everyone is asked what she is thankful for and the answers are the year in miniature. Sam says her guitar and her skateboard, and her family, she guesses. Kent says seeing her little one happy and healthy. Harvey says the clinic and her patients' good health and then something more personal. Leah says a simple life. Maru says a loving family. Shane, asked directly, stalls, and then says she is thankful someone pulled her out of the gutter and showed her that life is worth living. George calls the whole thing humbug over a star and would rather be indoors. Pierre is delighted by the sales figures and wonders aloud whether she could invent more holidays. Caroline has had too much nog. Pam is still sore about losing the ice fishing contest. Sebastian is fulfilling family obligations and admits it is nice to have everyone together for once. Penny asks what gift you are hoping for and takes your answer seriously even when you are joking.

## Roleplay notes

The emotionally richest festival and the one that most rewards being played straight. The gift exchange is a ready-made scene: a specific person, a specific object, a public moment, and everyone watching what she does with her face. Loneliness is visible here in a way it is not the rest of the year — the tables, the families, the invitations extended and refused. Who is paired with whom is never fixed. Neither is whether a gift lands.

lore.name: Festival of Ice
lore.keys: festival of ice, ice fishing, winter 8, snowman, ice sculpture, frozen lake, lễ hội băng, hội băng, câu cá trên băng, người tuyết, tượng băng, hồ đóng băng
lore.content:
# Festival of Ice

## What it is

Winter 8, out on the frozen lake in the forest near Marnie's land, morning until mid-afternoon. A celebration of winter, which in practice means everyone standing about in the cold building things out of snow while a fishing contest happens on the ice. There is no food at all. Gus apologises for that and tells everyone to wait for the Winter Star, when they will be stuffed for days.

Robin carves the ice — parapets and sculpture — and asks not to be interrupted, because it needs her whole attention; she calls ice a rewarding challenge and a material she is not used to. Leah works alongside her and talks about impermanence being what makes the art better, and about tempering ice before you cut it or you cannot shape it at all. A travelling merchant sets up a stall with winter furniture, a rarecrow, hot food, and a Winter Star tree for anyone thinking ahead.

Everyone else makes snowmen. Emily gives hers a top hat and a scarf and insists it has to look the part. Abigail makes a snow-goon and wants your opinion of it. Maru says she is not creative about snowmen and then explains the engineering of a level foundation. Penny will ask what kind you should build together and go along with whatever you say, unless you tell her to think outside the box, in which case she will politely stay conventional. Sam and Vincent build one together and Sam gets defensive if you laugh before it is finished. Clint cannot get the snow to form balls and concludes she is better in heat. Evelyn makes one with Alex and says out loud that this could be the last time, and that life is short.

## The ice fishing contest

Holes are cut in the ice and the lake is stocked. Two minutes, provided rods, and whoever lands the most fish wins. The mayor explains the rules twice, says *begin*, and the whistle goes.

Willy nearly always wins, and everyone knows it. Pam enters every year, takes it more seriously than she takes most things, blames her spot when she loses, and says Willy is impossible to beat because she does this day and night. Elliott enters to be sporting, is frankly bad at it, and does not mind; she brings a flask of spirits to sip just before the whistle and calls it her secret weapon. Sebastian has money on the outcome with Marlon. Marlon rates Willy a tough competitor and asks whether you think you can beat her.

When it is over the mayor gags at the smell of the pile, hands over the prize, thanks everyone for coming, and tells them to put the poor fish back.

## Who else is where

Evelyn tells the story of how she met George at this festival — George threw a snowball at her, then came over to check she was all right, which Evelyn has counted as good manners for sixty years and treats as the origin of the marriage. George grumbles about being dragged into the cold and about needing a warm hat now she is old and bald. Linus builds an igloo and explains that she learned it from tundra dwellers beyond the frozen sea many years ago, and that an igloo makes a fine home but her tent is easier. Sebastian says she never gets cold and means it. Jodi says the cold brings people together. Kent likes winter because it is peaceful. Marnie feels sorry for all the cold animals out there and, some years, thinks the bundled-up piglet is adorable. Haley brings her camera for the light. Abigail lets slip that she is wearing the Winter Star sweater under her coat and asks you not to tell Pierre, who has bought the whole family matching ones.

## Roleplay notes

Cold, bright, and companionable — the festival with the least at stake and the most standing around, which makes it the easiest place for a long conversation. Two women building one snowman is a scene. Losing the contest is normal; winning it against Willy is a real event. The lake is frozen and Penny will not walk on it, which is worth remembering before anyone suggests it.

lore.name: Flower Dance
lore.keys: flower dance, spring 24, flower queen, dance partner, the clearing, lễ hội hoa, điệu nhảy hoa, vũ hội hoa, nữ hoàng hoa, bạn nhảy, khoảng rừng trống
lore.content:
# Flower Dance

## What it is

Spring 24, in a clearing in Cindersap Forest west of town, morning until mid-afternoon. Late spring, everything in bloom, a stream running past, and the whole valley standing about in a meadow being awkward. Evelyn spends a week on the floral arrangements and asks everyone whether they like them. There is sweet wine, a red jelly that gets discussed at length, and a dandelion salad Gus makes on the spot.

The dance itself is a formal partnered set — two facing lines, a fixed sequence of steps, slow and stilted and a bit ridiculous. The older women adore it. Everyone under forty finds it excruciating and does it anyway.

## Partners, and the trouble with them

You have to ask someone. That is the whole social engine of the day: a public, standing request that everyone can see being made and being answered. Refusals happen. So do accepted invitations that surprise both women involved. Anyone without a partner stands at the edge, and there is no polite way to disguise it.

The mayor explains the rule to anyone new — find a partner if you want to be in it — and then waits to be told the ceremony can begin.

## Who is where

Haley has been flower queen five years running, is practising her steps in the grass, and has no intention of stepping off the throne; Emily eventually decides to compete for the title and has been working on choreography. Abigail hates dancing in front of everyone and comes because Caroline makes her. Penny is visibly terrified. Clint stands alone watching Emily and wondering whether she would say yes, then drowns it in jelly. Marnie says out loud that love is in the air and she is still single, and separately, quietly, that she thinks Lewis is going to ask her. Marlon, at the edge as usual, notices Marnie looks lovely today. Sebastian did not come by choice. Kent finds the open field unsettling and whispers herself calm. Harvey works up the courage all morning. Sam admits she genuinely likes flowers. Leah is glad you came. Caroline wishes Pierre would spend the day with the family instead of the till, and Pierre cannot bear to leave the register.

Evelyn used to come here earlier in life and says it has not changed. Demetrius traces the whole thing to ancient fertility rites and tells you that you ought to know about this. Linus brings jelly she made from the berries and offers it round. Pam is delighted: wine, warm air, a babbling brook, and did she mention wine.

## Roleplay notes

The most emotionally loaded festival of the year and the easiest to use. A dance invitation is a small public declaration, and the answer is real — accept, refuse, hesitate, ask someone else first. Nothing forces a partner and nobody is owed one. The clearing is also large, the trees are close, and people wander off. Who is flower queen is not fixed and neither is whether anyone bothers with the title that year.

lore.name: Luau
lore.keys: luau, potluck, summer 11, the soup, communal soup, governor, tiệc luau, tiệc góp món, nồi súp, súp chung, thị trưởng, tỉnh trưởng
lore.content:
# Luau

## What it is

Summer 11, on the beach, morning until mid-afternoon. Hot sand, music loud enough that George complains about it, a buffet Gus has been cooking for days, torches and greenery strung along the pier, and sand flies landing on everything. The valley in as little clothing as it can justify, dancing badly on sand.

## The soup

The point of the day. A cauldron stands up the steps on the far side of the beach and everyone brings one ingredient to put in it — anything they grew, caught, made, or found. Then the regional governor, who visits once a year for exactly this, tastes it first while the entire town watches.

The mayor is unbearable about it. She fusses over the quality of what people contributed, reminds everyone the governor is a distinguished guest, and asks the town to be on its best behaviour. Penny explains it plainly to anyone new: this whole festival exists to give the governor a taste of what the valley can do, and the mayor is desperate to be liked, which is why she is so neurotic about the soup.

The tasting goes however it goes. Some years the governor calls it the best soup she has ever tasted and the mayor takes a bowl herself and beams. Some years it is bland and the mayor has to agree. Some years someone has ruined it with something foul and the governor turns grey and has to lie down, and the mayor stands there ashamed of the whole community and sends everyone home. And once, memorably, something extremely private of the mayor's was found floating in it, which ended the festival on the spot and is still the funniest thing that has ever happened here to everyone except her.

The governor herself is warm about the place, says the valley is a joy to visit, and keeps threatening to talk to her wife about buying a holiday house here. The town has heard the rumour and cannot decide whether it wants her.

Sam is the reigning suspect for every prank ever pulled on the pot — she once put a pound of anchovies in it — and Sebastian will tell you that is why Sam leads the town in community service hours.

## Who is where

Emily dances until she cannot speak and is completely lost in it. Robin and Demetrius dance and step on each other, and Demetrius asks whether she is ready to visit the buffet yet; Robin tells her it is because it is *fun*. Marnie stays off the pier and directs contributions to the cauldron from the sand. Linus is up the beach doing a slow, careful spit-roast and will explain that continuous rotation is the whole secret; Leo watches her do it and learns. Abigail finds socialising exhausting and would rather sit and watch the sea. Haley refuses to dance because she does not want to sweat, and stays exactly where the sun is best. Alex wants to swim but will not be the only one in the water. Pierre works the governor for a tax break the moment the mayor steps away and wonders whether she likes whiskey. Caroline puts her own vegetables in the pot and asks what you brought. Elliott, whose cabin is on this beach, woke up late and walked out into the middle of it having forgotten the day entirely. Willy would rather be fishing. Marlon stays back in the tree shade where it is cooler, watching the water in case something comes out of it.

The Wizard turns up somewhere she should not be and mentions that the merpeople are curious about the festivities and get upset when the town litters into the ocean.

## Roleplay notes

Heat, skin, drink, and one public ceremony that can go gloriously right or humiliatingly wrong. Good for prank plots, for the mayor's vanity, and for the fact that half the town is undressed in daylight in front of people they see every day. The soup's outcome is never fixed. Neither is whether the governor comes, whether anyone sabotages it, or whether the mayor survives the afternoon with her dignity.

lore.name: Dance of the Moonlight Jellies
lore.keys: moonlight jellies, dance of the moonlight jellies, summer 28, candle boat, jellyfish, sứa phát sáng, đêm sứa, sứa dưới ánh trăng, điệu nhảy của sứa phát sáng, thuyền nến, con sứa
lore.content:
# Dance of the Moonlight Jellies

## What it is

The last night of summer — summer 28 — on the beach, from ten at night. The whole valley walks down to the water in the dark and stands on the docks, and there is no buffet, no contest, no speech worth the name. The moonlight jellies pass Pelican Town once a year on their way south, and the town goes out to meet them.

Robin builds and maintains the candle-boat and checks it for holes every year, because imagine if it sank during the festival. The mayor launches it off the end of the dock and the town watches the candles go out across the black water. Then, some minutes later, the jellies come: a faint glow on the horizon, and then the whole shallows lit blue from underneath.

Everyone goes quiet. That is the actual event. Thirty women standing on old wood in the dark, saying nothing.

## What it means here

Demetrius will tell you the species is remarkable and that nobody knows why they follow light. The Wizard, tucked somewhere she should not be, calls them Lunaloos and says they carry an unusually strong magical aura for anything aquatic; she is here to observe them and is faintly annoyed to be found. Willy says the old rule is that if you ever hook one you throw her straight back. There is supposed to be a rare green one, and Abigail intends to be the first to see it every year. Jas hopes for babies.

The rest of it is a summer ending in front of everyone. Leah pays her respects to another bygone summer and means it. Alex cannot believe it went so fast. Maru notices the cold and says fall is right around the corner. Harvey is glad to see the back of the mosquitos. Pierre reminds people to come in for fall seeds tomorrow, which is exactly as romantic as she is. Evelyn saw the jellies decades ago and jumped for joy, and says she has less of that in her now, and she and George have watched them come and go together for decades. Caroline says the candles are romantic. Marnie will not walk out onto the dock — the creaking is enough, and she fell through a rotten one earlier in life — so she stays back on the sand. Marlon takes the dark seriously and watches it with her one good eye.

Sebastian claims she saw something big moving out there and admits she is only trying to frighten you. Sam wonders whether they sting and reconsiders pushing Sebastian in. Elliott, whose cabin is fifty yards away, talks about ocean pollution and what will happen to the jellies eventually, and is not wrong. Linus waits until the jellies arrive and then slips down quietly to a dock nobody is using, because she likes watching them too and does not want to be in the way.

## Roleplay notes

The most romantic hour in the calendar and it costs nothing to use: full dark, cold air off the water, a crowd all facing the same direction and none of them looking at each other. People bring blankets. People stand closer than they would at noon. Two women can have an entire conversation here that neither could have in the square, and blue light on skin does most of the work. Pair it with the end of something — a summer, a job, a pretence.

lore.name: Night Market
lore.keys: night market, winter 15, winter 16, winter 17, merchant fleet, submarine, chợ đêm, phiên chợ đêm, đội thuyền buôn, tàu ngầm, chợ trên bãi biển
lore.content:
# Night Market

## What it is

Winter 15, 16 and 17, on the beach and the pier, from five in the evening until late. A fleet of travelling merchants puts in at Pelican Town for three nights and turns the dark beach into a lit market. It is the newest tradition here and the town took to it fast. The notice promises free coffee, which is most of why some people come.

Boats moor along the pier with lanterns strung between them and each one sells something different. One deals in outdoor decoration and asks whether anything catches your eye. One is unsettling — a blue-lit boat whose keeper speaks in a whisper and stocks something new every night, rare seeds, strange furniture, a piano — and Emily says it is her favourite because it is so unique. Even the travelling cart merchant who works the forest road comes by sea for this, and reports that her pig likes the swim. The desert trader shuts up shop and comes in for it.

## What there is to do

**The submarine.** A captain runs a deep-sea tour out of the end of the pier and takes people down for an hour of fishing in water nobody sees otherwise. Willy says the captain is an old friend. Demetrius highly recommends it and will tell you about the creatures at that depth. Maru is more interested in the machine than the fish. Sam decides that if everything else fails she will become a submarine captain, which might be cool.

**The mermaid show.** In a small house at the end of the beach, five performers put on a show by lamplight to a strange, slow song. Something is hidden in it — there is a crumpled note that circulates in the valley giving five numbers in a particular order and nothing else by way of explanation, and anyone who works out what to do with them gets something out of the sea for it. Alex says the show is her favourite thing about the whole market. Clint wants to see it to calm her nerves before a doctor's appointment and immediately panics about what people will think she is looking at. Jas is not old enough and says so sadly.

**The painter.** A woman who introduces herself as the famous painter Lupini sells exactly one canvas a night for twelve hundred gold and will not sell you a second. Leah studies one and allows that a Lupini original is not bad.

**A shrouded figure** at the edge of the light will send you home for two hundred and fifty gold and does not explain how.

## Who is where

Caroline does all her winter shopping here and asks you to warn her if you see Pierre coming. Marnie finds fine purple silk and points out you cannot get that at the warehouse store. Lewis says she has bought some of her favourite things at this market. Robin loves the boats themselves and the creaking of wet wood. Sebastian is more relaxed at night and might even buy a trinket. Penny stands in the spiced air and asks if you can smell it. Harvey says winter is a dreary season and this makes it brighter. Abigail finds the whole thing mysterious and loves it. Evelyn calls it one of the newer traditions and asks George whether they have not taken to it rather quickly; George is there for the free coffee. Elliott is enchanted by the idea of a merchant fleet travelling the world for riches. Jodi sighs about how thrilling it must be. Linus feels a kinship with them as fellow travellers and is content to stand and watch. Leo just likes looking at the lights, and says it reminds her of something long ago. Shane takes the night off the saloon for Jas's sake.

Willy cannot sleep with the market going on right outside her shop, and shrugs it off — she is flexible — and on the third night says there is nothing like a hot drink after a cold, dark day.

## Roleplay notes

Three consecutive evenings of lantern light, cold sand, unfamiliar merchants, and a town out after dark with money to spend. The best-lit romantic setting in the calendar after the jellies and far less solemn. Good for buying someone something, for the submarine as an hour alone underwater, for the mermaid show as a shared secret, and for the fact that nobody is where they usually are. Nothing has to be bought and nothing has to be found.

lore.name: Spirit's Eve
lore.keys: spirit's eve, spirits eve, fall 27, haunted maze, halloween, jack-o-lantern, đêm ma quái, đêm linh hồn, lễ hội ma, mê cung ma, đèn bí ngô
lore.content:
# Spirit's Eve

## What it is

Fall 27, the town square, from ten at night. The mayor's letter says there is a chill in the air and it may be the approach of winter or it may be the tingle of a dark specter come to help the town celebrate, which is the most theatrical she gets all year. The square goes up in jack-o-lanterns, gravestones, and green-lit fog, and the town comes out in the dark to eat pumpkin food, drink pumpkin ale, and frighten itself.

Emily carves the pumpkins she is proud of; Gus does most of the town's lanterns and asks only to keep the seeds, which she sugars and eats. Caroline buys a pumpkin off whoever has one to carve with Abigail. There is a cauldron with something in it giving off vapour that makes people who stand near it lightheaded and reluctant to leave — Penny cannot make herself walk away from it and says her head is spinning; the fumes make other people unusually forward.

## The maze

The Wizard builds a haunted maze in secret every year and lets nobody near it while she works. She will tell you, if you find her, that the affairs of ordinary folk matter little to her but the elementals like a chance to see the town up close, and it was for them that she made the silly thing. Lewis knows only that the strange woman from the tower set it all up herself.

Inside are dead ends that were not dead ends a moment ago, walking skeletons nobody can explain, grasping hands, spiders, and — for anyone who gets all the way through — a golden pumpkin, which is valuable and useless. It gets larger every year. Linus goes in and comes out saying *good show, old friend*, because the two of them understand each other. Some people never find the middle. Abigail cannot go on: spiders. Haley is too scared to enter at all. Maru gets thoroughly lost and insists she has almost worked it out. Harvey hides in a corner because she got frightened and asks you not to tell anyone. Sam swears someone was walking ahead of her and then was not.

Outside the maze, Marlon has brought caged monsters and tells everyone to mind their distance. Clint says one of her iridium maces would make short work of the skeletons. Pierre runs a stall selling gravestones and lanterns and is quietly furious about missing the party.

## Who is where

Jodi will not let Vincent into the maze and Vincent sobs about it; some years Sam takes her in anyway and they get stuck. Jas begs Marnie and Marnie says no, and one year Shane talks her into it and takes Jas through very slowly. Pam is there for free food and will not go near the maze. Leah has had too much pumpkin ale and admits it. Shane wants to know why there is no more pumpkin ale. Robin thinks about stockpiling wood before winter. Evelyn wishes, as at the fair, that there were zucchini fritters. George eats the smoked turkey and concedes the festival is not all bad. Demetrius reports a study about music and cortisol and then asks whether there is ice cream for the cobbler. Elliott addresses the caged monsters in verse and says that sometimes one must stare into the abyss to stir a sluggish muse.

The shadow-dweller from the sewers comes up one year, is startled to be seen, and asks what you are doing here.

## Roleplay notes

Dark, costumed, crowded, and slightly drunk — the festival that gives everyone permission. Fear is a legitimate excuse to hold onto someone. The maze separates people from the crowd and puts them somewhere enclosed with no witnesses, which is the entire point of it. The vapour is a good device and needs no explanation. Nothing about the maze is fixed: it can be terrifying, silly, genuinely dangerous, or empty of anything but the Wizard's showmanship.

lore.keys: stardew valley fair, the fair, fall 16, grange display, star tokens, fortune teller, hội chợ thung lũng, hội chợ, gian trưng bày, quầy trưng bày, xu ngôi sao, người xem tướng
lore.content:
# Stardew Valley Fair

## What it is

Fall 16, the town square, morning until mid-afternoon, and the largest thing that happens here all year. The mayor writes a week in advance rather than a day, because there is work to do. Tents go up over the whole square, tourists come in by bus from across the country, and Pelican Town spends one day being looked at by strangers and enjoying it enormously.

There is barbecue all day and it is free, compliments of the mayor — Gus works four grills at once, puts her sauce in everything, and refuses to say what is in it no matter who asks. Animals are brought in and penned: chickens, cows and calves, pigs, rabbits, sheep, goats. Everything is louder than the town normally is.

## The grange displays

The competition that matters. Each business or household sets out its best nine things in a stand and is judged on quality and variety, and the mayor leaves an empty stand for anyone new. Pierre has been setting aside her finest produce for weeks and is completely serious about winning. Caroline supplies part of it out of her own glasshouse and has been growing for this all year. Marnie knows her display is weaker than Pierre's and hopes the judges give her something for the enormous cheese wheel. Clint lays out her best pieces, tells you she takes real pride in her work, and asks you to look closely. Willy brings iridium-quality fish. Robin's woodwork is there and she calls the craft an ancient tradition she is proud to be part of; Leah admires it openly and uses the same techniques in her own work, and the two of them end up teaching each other.

Judging is public. First place gets a rating read out, a ribbon, and a thousand star tokens; the lower places get less and a suggestion to try again next year. The mayor reminds every single winner to go and clean out her box.

## The games

Star tokens are the fair's currency, sold at fifty a piece and won at the tents. A slingshot range. A wheel of chance where you wager tokens and lose them — Sam bets and loses everything and says she should have gone green. A strength machine that rates you on a scale running from *plankton* and *wet tissue* up through *George's knee* and *soggy spaghetti* to *bodybuilder*, *mountain troll* and *mammoth*; Alex plays it until her arms give out and eats a sandwich for every hundred rounds. A fishing tent Elliott comes out of smelling of fish and delighted with a personal best. Penny won the wheel ten times running one year and is no longer allowed to play.

The token stall trades for prizes: a rarecrow, a hat, a rug, a dried sunflower arrangement, seeds, and — for anyone who has never bought one before — a stardrop.

## The fortune teller

Welwick sets her stand up in the graveyard, of all places, and reads fortunes for a hundred gold. She is a genuine diviner with a television show and the Wizard's professional respect — the two have known each other a long time and the Wizard calls her a good friend and a remarkable one. What she gives people is uncomfortably specific: a crystal ball view of who you will end up beside, whether you are playing games with people who trust you, whether you end up alone in a plush chair surrounded by luxury and desperation. She tells Haley something *interesting* and Haley giggles about it all day. Sebastian comes away from her stand not knowing what to make of it. She reads one couple's future as a happy life together. She always finishes by saying the future is not set in stone and can still be changed if you set your heart on it, and once she has read you she will not read you again — she says so rudely.

## Who else is where

There is a clown, hired on a budget, and she is not funny; Jodi assumes the mayor cut costs, Kent waits for her to do something and is disappointed, Emily thinks she would have made a better one and may have missed her calling, and the Wizard studies her and says she knows her from somewhere — the school of illusion, perhaps, or the Carnival of Secrets.

Tourists wander about being pleasant and eating too much: the biggest cheese wheel they have ever seen, a long bus ride but worth it, a fine-looking town with a real sense of community. Some of them litter and Jodi takes it personally. Sandy shuts the Oasis and travels in for the day, which is one of the few times Emily gets to see her. Shane has the animals fed and content and tells anyone to go ahead and pet them. Linus watches the animals and observes that they never judge anyone by their looks, which is more than she can say for people. Marlon has come to look at Clint's blades, which get sharper every year, along with her prices. Evelyn wishes there were a vegetarian option and suggests zucchini skewers. Harvey stands two steps from a rack of pork ribs having a crisis of professional conscience.

## Roleplay notes

Crowded, loud, competitive, and full of strangers — the best day of the year for a chance encounter, a rivalry, a public embarrassment, or a fortune that lands too close to the bone. The grange result is never fixed and neither is who wins what. Welwick is a good device precisely because she says the thing a character is refusing to say, and then leaves.
